original_question: For which values of k and d is the following true: if a k-orbit d-polytope P is realized as a convex d-polytope, then P must be isomorphic to a geometrically k-orbit convex polytope?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1 in Section 1 (Introduction): whether every combinatorially k-orbit convex d-polytope is, up to abstract isomorphism, a geometrically k-orbit convex d-polytope; with nearby clarification from Proposition 1.2 and the dimensional restrictions from Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core implication of the paper’s introductory conjecture: starting from a k-orbit abstract d-polytope that is realizable as a convex d-polytope, it asks whether one can always find a convex realization whose geometric symmetry also has exactly k flag-orbits. It also correctly treats k and d as the governing parameters.
missing_details: It should say explicitly that P is an abstract d-polytope and that 'k-orbit' means that the automorphism group Aut(P) has exactly k orbits on the flags.
It should specify that 'realized as a convex d-polytope' means that P is isomorphic, as an abstract polytope, to the face lattice of a convex d-dimensional polytope in Euclidean space.
It should define 'geometrically k-orbit convex polytope' in terms of the Euclidean symmetry group acting with exactly k flag-orbits.

It should clarify that the conclusion is existence of some geometrically k-orbit convex d-polytope abstractly isomorphic to P, not that every convex realization of P must already have k geometric flag-orbits.
It should make the quantifiers explicit: for fixed integers k and d, determine whether the implication holds for every such P.
It should keep the scope narrow to convex d-polytopes, not skeletal polytopes, tilings, or non-convex realizations.
It should use the paper’s combinatorial-vs-geometric symmetry language; otherwise the role of flag-orbits and the distinction between automorphism group and Euclidean symmetry group remain implicit.

No ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or 'sufficiently large' asymptotic clause is part of this problem; the missing information is instead about polytope type, group action, realization, and isomorphism.
refined_question: For which integers k and d does the following hold: whenever an abstract d-polytope P has exactly k flag-orbits under its automorphism group and is isomorphic to the face lattice of a convex d-dimensional polytope, there exists a convex d-polytope Q whose Euclidean symmetry group has exactly k flag-orbits and whose face lattice is isomorphic to P?
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper’s introductory conjecture on combinatorial versus geometric symmetry for convex realizations. Conjecture 1.1 is the nearest official formulation. The surrounding introductory context, together with Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3, shows that the intended question is not about arbitrary realizations or broader geometric objects, but specifically about abstract d-polytopes, convex d-dimensional realizations, and equality of the number of combinatorial and geometric flag-orbits up to abstract isomorphism. Theorem 1.3 provides the relevant geometric dimension bounds for fixed k, which is why k and d are the right external parameters, but the main target remains the implication stated in Conjecture 1.1.
